{{short description|German laser physicist and educator (born 1946)}}
'''Ludger Wöste''' (born 2 May 1946 in [[Emsbüren]]) is a German physicist and professor at the [[Free University of Berlin]]. He is known for research in laser control of chemistry and laser-based weather control through the creation of [[plasma channel]]s by laser filamentation in air.<ref name=speaker>{{Cite web |title=Photoptics 2015 speakers |url=https://photoptics.scitevents.org/KeynoteSpeakers.aspx?y=2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kasparian |first1=Jérôme |last2=Wöste |first2=Ludger |last3=Wolf |first3=Jean-Pierre |date=2010-07-01 |title=Laser-Based Weather Control |url=https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?URI=opn-21-7-22 |journal=Optics and Photonics News |language=en |volume=21 |issue=7 |pages=22 |doi=10.1364/OPN.21.7.000022 |bibcode=2010OptPN..21...22K |issn=1047-6938|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Wöste studied physics and electrical engineering at the [[RWTH Aachen University]] from 1965, then physics at the [[University of Bonn]] from 1968. He completed his diploma under [[Herbert Walther]] in 1972, on the deflection of a sodium atom beam in the radiation field of a dye laser.

From 1973 to 1978 he worked as an assistant to Ernst Schumacher at the [[University of Bern]], receiving his doctorate in 1978 for work on mass selective laser spectroscopy on metal atom clusters. He then spent time as a postdoc with [[Richard N. Zare]] at [[Stanford University]] until 1980, studying laser chemistry (reactions on optically oriented molecules).

From 1980 to 1987 he was a project manager (photodynamic behavior of metal clusters) and lecturer at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne]], serving as head of research for laser applications from 1981. In 1984, he was a visiting professor at the Aimé Cotton Laboratory of the [[University of Paris-Sud]], where he studied the transition from non-conducting to conducting metal in mercury clusters. 

From 1989 he was a professor at the [[Free University of Berlin]], and from 2007 to 2008 he served as dean of the physics department. Since 2014 he has been Wilhelm and Else Heraeus Senior Professor for new teaching concepts in physics.<ref name=speaker />

== Research ==
Wöste's research focuses on the applications of laser spectroscopy and laser chemistry, including the aspects of [[Ultrafast laser spectroscopy|ultrafast spectroscopy]], catalysis, clusters, optical remote sensing of the atmosphere, He's also known for developments in physics education - among other things he developed a construction kit for demonstration experiments at schools around mass spectrometry and the laser.

In the 2000s, along with his former PhD student [[Jean-Pierre Wolf]], Wöste and colleagues constructed the world's first mobile terawatt laser system, Teramobile.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wille |first1=H. |last2=Rodriguez |first2=M. |last3=Kasparian |first3=J. |last4=Mondelain |first4=D. |last5=Yu |first5=J. |last6=Mysyrowicz |first6=A. |last7=Sauerbrey |first7=R. |last8=Wolf |first8=J. P. |last9=Wöste |first9=L. |date=2002 |title=Teramobile: A mobile femtosecond-terawatt laser and detection system |url=https://www.epjap.org/articles/epjap/abs/2002/12/ap01224/ap01224.html |journal=The European Physical Journal Applied Physics |language=en |volume=20 |issue=3 |pages=183–190 |doi=10.1051/epjap:2002090 |bibcode=2002EPJAP..20..183W |issn=1286-0042|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Teramobile press book |url=https://www.teramobile.org/press_short.html}}</ref> The goal of the project is to induce rainfall through intense laser-induced filamentation in air.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rohwetter |first1=Philipp |last2=Kasparian |first2=Jérôme |last3=Stelmaszczyk |first3=Kamil |last4=Hao |first4=Zuoqiang |last5=Henin |first5=Stefano |last6=Lascoux |first6=Noëlle |last7=Nakaema |first7=Walter M. |last8=Petit |first8=Yannick |last9=Queißer |first9=Manuel |last10=Salamé |first10=Rami |last11=Salmon |first11=Estelle |last12=Wöste |first12=Ludger |last13=Wolf |first13=Jean-Pierre |date=2010 |title=Laser-induced water condensation in air |url=http://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2010.115 |journal=Nature Photonics |language=en |volume=4 |issue=7 |pages=451–456 |doi=10.1038/nphoton.2010.115 |bibcode=2010NaPho...4..451R |issn=1749-4885|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Wöste received the Marian Smoluchowski and Emil Warburg Prize for Physics in 1999<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wöste |first=Ludger |date=1999 |title=Marian Smoluchowski-Emil Warburg-Preis: Laudatio auf den Preisträger 1999 |journal=Physik Journal |language=de |volume=55 |issue=6 |pages=60 |doi=10.1002/phbl.19990550616|s2cid=121509391 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the [[Gay-Lussac–Humboldt Prize|Gay-Lussac-Humboldt Prize]] in 2006. In 2004, he was honorary professor at [[Nanjing University]]. In 2007, he became a knight of the [[Ordre national du Mérite]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Ludger Wöste |url=https://www.schule-mit-wissenschaft.de/archiv/bundeskonferenzen/berlin-2019/prof-dr-ludger-woeste/ |access-date=2023-01-05 |website=Schule mit Wissenschaft |language=de-DE}}</ref>

Wöste holds honorary doctorates from the [[West University of Timișoara]] and the [[University of Lyon|University of Lyon I]]. Wöste holds 13 patents and has over 320 scientific publications.
